unit: $/m2 of finished 150mm slab, measured on plan, Auckland Q3 2026, subcontract rate, GST exclusive

band.unit: $/m2 of finished 150mm slab, measured on plan, Auckland Q3 2026, subcontract rate, GST exclusive
band.basis: Sum of the 16 components above (QV Auckland rates x measured quantities + 4 minor labelled allowances). 300 m2 total: low $43,800, high $62,100, centre $52,800. Quantities used: 300 m2, 45 m3 concrete (0.15m + 5% waste), 70 lm perimeter, 120 lm sawcut control joints at 4.0m centres, 20 lm isolation joint, one 45 m3 pour. Cross-check: QV's composite 'Concrete Slab on Ground 150mm' row f0968d722af3d033d91c79c47fe7ecbea989e5abaecc3422c66d853ac075ca53:t3:r3 (AKL 199/m2) adjusted to this scope lands at ~$215/m2, above the component sum - the ~$25/m2 difference is placing/vibrating labour that may or may not sit inside QV's hand-finish rows, which is why the top of the band is held wide and confidence is medium. If SE92 is taken literally as the specified mesh (QV row AKL 52/m2) the band narrows to $175-$207/m2; if the '665 grade' wording is read as the light 150x150x5.3 mesh (AKL 20.3/m2) it is $146-$175/m2. Allowances total $5.5-$12.5/m2, about 4-6% of the band, so the band is not allowance-driven. QV rows are unreviewed and no Q3 2026 escalation has been applied to them.

band.unit: $/m2 of finished slab (Auckland, Q3 2026, subcontract, GST exclusive; 300 m2 total in brackets)
band.basis: Sum of 11 distinct components, each priced from cited QV CostBuilder rows (Auckland column) or a labelled allowance. No component is counted twice: the 150mm paving rate (item 4) carries the concrete, placing, screed, broomed finish, curing, edge formwork and nominal mesh, so QR formwork, curing-compound and mesh rows are used only as deltas or not at all; the hardfill, pump and joints are priced separately because the paving rate does not itemise them. 300 m2 total = $63,960 - $70,200, midpoint $67,100. Midpoint $224/m2. Confidence medium because the anchoring QV paving rate does not itemise inclusions: if it excludes mesh and edge formwork entirely add up to ~$20-30/m2 (upper end ~$260/m2); if it includes a basecourse/sand bed, deduct ~$17/m2. Allowances (trim/cart spoil, set out, wood float edges) are ~4% of the total, well under a third.

Auckland, Q3 2026, subcontract rate, GST exclusive. Sum of the ten components above: low $156.3/m2, high $266.2/m2, midpoint $211/m2. 300 m2 total: $46,900 low, $79,900 high, $63,400 midpoint. The spread is dominated by two QV-consistent but divergent routes to the same 150mm slab (External Works paving composite $144-147/m2 vs the QV component build about $89/m2) and by QV's SE92 mesh row ($52/m2, about $10.4/kg) against QV's own installed bar rate ($5.60/kg, giving about $29/m2 by weight). Only one component is an allowance (set-out, about 2% of the band). The scenario's own $148-192/m2 sits at the bottom of this envelope: it is reachable on the lighter 665 mesh reading, a trade concrete supply rate and efficient 300 m2 open-pour labour, but it is the optimistic end. QV measured rates may embed contractor overhead and profit, so the top of the band may double-count margin the scenario excludes. Confidence low.
